title: Build the mirror image of a model
instruction: Build the mirror image of the model on the grey plate, using the four loose cubes.
context: Left- and right-hand versions of a part are often built from a sample of the other; here the sample is a fixed model of four cubes.
setup: Coordinates: x forward from the line between the two arm bases, y to the left, from the midpoint between the bases. All cubes are 4 cm painted wooden cubes, axis-aligned. The model, glued to the table and to each other: red at (32, 22) cm and blue at (32, 18) cm side by side, yellow at (28, 18) cm in front of blue, green on top of red. A grey painted wooden build plate, 20 x 20 x 0.5 cm, taped to the table, centred at (30, -20) cm. Loose cubes, 50 g each, on the table: red at (16, 20) cm, green at (16, 10) cm, blue at (16, -24) cm, yellow at (14, -15) cm.
scoring: The build may stand anywhere on the build plate, turned any way about the vertical. 0.5 if red, blue and yellow stand on the plate (centres over the plate, within 1 cm of 2 cm above its top) and, after the best-fitting turn about the vertical and shift (no reflection), each centre is within 1.5 cm of its place in the mirror image's base (blue left of red, both 4 cm apart; yellow 4 cm in front of blue). 1.0 if, in addition, green's centre is within 1.5 cm horizontally of red's and 4 cm (within 1 cm) higher; the trial ends once that holds with every cube at rest (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s. 0 otherwise; a copy of the model that is not mirrored scores 0 at any position and angle, as does anything built off the plate.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed; put the four loose cubes back at their starting positions.
fidelity: Approximate: rigid cubes with PhysX default friction; the model's glued cubes and the taped plate are fixed bodies.
